description: A2UI component catalog — the single contract shared by the backend composer (which is told these components and asked to emit one of these surfaces) and the frontend registry renderer (which has a React component for each). Add a component here + a renderer in the frontend registry to extend; no other code changes are needed.

Markdown.summary: A block of GitHub-flavored markdown (headings, lists, tables, code, links).

Text.summary: A short run of plain text.

Card.summary: A titled container that groups child components. Optionally set 'icon' to a supported icon name (see the icon list in the rules).

KeyValue.summary: A single label/value pair; good for KPIs and metrics. Optionally set 'icon' to a supported icon name (see the icon list in the rules) for a pictographic accent.

List.summary: An ordered or unordered list of strings.

Table.summary: A data table. columns is a list of header strings; rows is a list of row arrays (cell values aligned to columns).

Grid.summary: Lays out children in a responsive grid with the given column count.

Chart.summary: A chart. data is a list of row objects; xKey names the category field; yKeys names the numeric series field(s). chartType: 'bar' (comparisons), 'line' (trends over time), 'pie' (parts of a whole), 'area' (cumulative/volume trends), 'scatter' (correlation between two numeric fields), 'radar' (multi-dimension profile comparison).

Mindmap.summary: A mindmap / tree. root is a node object of shape {id, label, description?, children:[node...]}. Give EVERY node a short label AND a one-sentence 'description' explaining it (shown as a hover tooltip). Use as the root for surfaceKind 'mindmap'.

Quiz.summary: An interactive multiple-choice quiz / assessment. questions is a list of REAL questions, each of shape {question, options:[4 strings], answer:<0-based index of the correct option>, explanation?}. The renderer handles option selection, immediate right/wrong reveal, scoring and navigation — supply ONLY the question data, never a description of a quiz. Use as the root for surfaceKind 'quiz'.

Flashcards.summary: An interactive Anki-style flashcard deck for studying. cards is a list of REAL study cards, each of shape {front, back, hint?}. front is the prompt/question shown first; back is the answer revealed on flip. The renderer handles flipping (click to reveal), deck navigation and shuffle — supply ONLY the card data, never a description of a deck. Use as the root for surfaceKind 'flashcards'.

Map.summary: A geographic map that plots points from coordinates. points is a list of {lat, lng, label?, value?}. Use ONLY when the data has real latitude/longitude coordinates. The renderer draws a lightweight world map with the points and a legend. Use as the root for surfaceKind 'map'.

points.shape: [{ lat: number, lng: number, label, value }]

Forecast.summary: A time-series FORECAST chart: a forecast line plus an optional shaded confidence band and optional historical actuals. data is a list of row objects. The renderer AUTO-DETECTS the columns, so pass the query rows as-is; optionally set xKey (time/date column), forecastKey (the predicted value), lowerKey/upperKey (confidence band), actualKey (historical actuals), and seriesKey (a category column to split into one line per group, e.g. risk_category). Use for any prediction/forecast/projection over time with or without a confidence interval.

Graph.summary: A node-link GRAPH / network / relationship diagram. nodes is a list of {id, label?, group?}; edges a list of {from, to, label?} referencing node ids. Nodes are auto-laid-out on a circle and colored by 'group'. Set directed:false for undirected edges (default is directed with arrowheads). Use for dependencies, relationships, networks, entity links, org/flow structure — NOT for time series (use Chart/Forecast) or hierarchical trees (use Mindmap).

Sequence.summary: A UML-style SEQUENCE diagram. actors is an ordered list of participant names (or {id, label}); messages a list of {from, to, text?, dashed?} drawn top-to-bottom as arrows between actor lifelines (dashed:true for a return/async message). Use for interactions, request/response flows, protocols, call sequences over time between participants.

Album.summary: An image ALBUM shown as a one-image-at-a-time CAROUSEL with prev/next. items is a list of image URLs or {src, caption?, href?}. Use ONLY for real image URLs (src must be a direct image link). The caption links to href (or the source URL). Use for photo galleries / image collections — never for a list of non-image links (use a Table or List for those).

RegionHeatmap.summary: Regions shaded by value on a GRID — it shows which regions are high and low and by how much, but NOT where they are: there is no map geometry, no boundaries and no projection. Use for a per-region comparison (states, provinces, zones) where the ranking is the point. When the reader needs actual geography with coordinates, use Map instead.

regions.note: [{name, value, label?}] — one entry per region.

unit.note: Shown on the scale, e.g. GW or %.

Sankey.summary: A flow diagram: ribbons whose width is the quantity moving between stages. Columns are derived from the flows themselves, so supply a chain and it lays out left to right. Use for energy or material balances, budget allocation, conversion losses and funnels — anywhere the story is how much goes where.

flows.note: [{from, to, value}] — value must be positive.

Kanban.summary: A KANBAN project board with columns of swimlanes (e.g., To Do / In Progress / Done). columns is a list of {id, title, color?, cards?} where each card is {id, label, detail?, tag?, color?}. Use for task tracking, sprint boards, workflow visualization — NOT for tables (use Table) or charts (use Chart). The model should classify content into columns based on status/state and generate meaningful card labels from the data.

columns.shape: [{ id, title, color?, cards: [{ id, label, detail?, tag?, color? }] }]
